Even when we hit our sales targets, which used to be a huge deal for me, I just feel nothing. Thinking feels like wading through mud; my brain just gets tired so fast. There have been times, a few months ago actually, when things got really dark. I even started looking up ways to just… stop feeling this way, if that makes sense.

But then, for the past month, it's been the opposite. I have so much energy, I can barely sit still at work. I'm buzzing, talking a mile a minute, bouncing between customers and restocking, not feeling tired even if I've only slept a couple of hours. My team says I'm a bit snappier than usual, and I guess I do get annoyed easily these days. It’s not causing problems at work, but it’s definitely a shift. It’s mostly just this intense feeling of restlessness, like I have to be doing something constantly. It's confusing because sometimes I feel totally on edge during these bursts of energy, like I'm waiting for something bad to happen, but mostly I just feel really wound up.
D009-D011_h001.question_a:
Lately, I’ve been feeling like I’m on a seesaw, and it's exhausting. For about a month now, I’ve been so revved up. I find myself snapping at my employees over the tiniest things; it's like a switch flips and I just can’t control my irritation. I have this boundless energy, constantly pacing the store, reorganizing displays, and just needing to *do* something. Sleep? What’s that? I barely get a few hours, if any, and still wake up feeling completely refreshed, ready to tackle the day. My mouth just runs on and on, I can’t seem to stop talking during team meetings, often monopolizing the conversation. It's like my mind is buzzing with ideas, and I just have to get them all out. This increased energy and talkativeness are just part of who I am right now, and the thoughts rushing through my head feel separate from the mild anxiety I sometimes have about work.

But then, for the past year, it’s been the complete opposite. A heavy, dark cloud just hangs over me. I feel so incredibly down, and even when sales targets are smashed or I get praised for a new display, I just don't care. It’s like my achievements mean nothing. Simple tasks at work feel monumental; my mind just gives out after a few minutes of trying to concentrate. I even tried to end it all a few months ago. I remember hoarding some pills, thinking it was the only way out. It’s hard to even get out of bed sometimes, let alone run a store.
D009-D011_h001.question_b:

It's weird, I used to love hitting my sales targets, but lately, I just don't care. My brain feels so sluggish, like it takes all my energy just to think through simple tasks for work. A few months ago, it got so bad… I actually tried to overdose on some pills I’d saved up. I just wanted it all to stop.

But then, about a month ago, things got really hectic. I wasn't sleeping at all, like maybe an hour or two a night, and I felt buzzing with energy, ready to go. I'd be pacing around my apartment after closing, just needing to *do* something, anything – picking up clothes, organizing my makeup collection for hours. D009-D011_h004.question_both:
It’s been a rough year, doc. I feel like I'm constantly on a rollercoaster, and not the fun kind. For the past month, I’ve been incredibly on edge. Everything sets me off – a misplaced knife, a comment from a server – I just feel this rage bubbling up. And I can’t sit still. I’m always pacing, wiping down counters that are already clean, reorganizing the pantry for the tenth time. Sleep? What’s that? I barely get a few hours, then I’m up and going, feeling surprisingly energized, like I could conquer the world, just talking and talking to whoever will listen. My sous chefs probably think I’ve lost my mind.

But then, it just… crashes. For the past year, I’ve felt this overwhelming sadness, like a heavy blanket I can't shake off. I don’t even want to get out of bed most days, let alone plan new menus or get excited about a service. My energy is just gone. And if I’m honest, sometimes I just want it all to stop. I think about closing my eyes and it all being over, sometimes even coming up with ways I could make that happen. I know I shouldn’t, but it’s just… a thought that crosses my mind. It’s making it really hard to run the kitchen, to be the chef I know I can be. My divorce didn’t help with any of this, for sure.
D009-D011_h004.question_a:
"Lately, it feels like I'm on a rollercoaster I can't get off. For the past year, I’ve been plunged into this deep sadness. It’s not just a bad mood; it’s a constant gloom that hangs over me. I used to love the hustle of the kitchen, but now, I have no motivation to even start prepping for service, let alone finish a complex dish. My energy is just nonexistent; getting through the day feels like wading through thick mud. Honestly, there are times I’ve pictured exactly how I could just end it, down to the last detail, and it’s been incredibly hard to function.

Then, for about a month, things flipped. I wasn’t sleeping – maybe two or three hours a night – but I felt unbelievably refreshed, full of buzzing energy. I’d be talking a mile a minute, explaining recipes, ideas, anything, and just couldn't stop. I felt incredibly restless, constantly pacing the kitchen, hands flying, unable to sit still for a second. Even though I felt this intense drive, it didn't really get in the way of my work; if anything, I got a lot done, even if I was a bit snappier with the junior chefs.

It's weird, because I do get anxious, especially about deadlines and the restaurant’s reputation. But even when I'm feeling that restless energy or my mind is racing with ideas, the anxiety doesn't feel like the source of it. It’s like the racing thoughts and the impulsivity just happen on their own, separate from the anxious worries that sometimes creep in."
D009-D011_h004.question_b:
"Lately, I just can't seem to relax. For the past year, I've been in a continuous slump – a deep sadness that just won't lift. Getting out of bed feels like trudging through quicksand, and the thought of firing up the kitchen at work... it's a monumental effort. My energy is completely zapped, and even simple tasks feel impossible. There are days I meticulously plan how I could just end it all, mapping out scenarios in my head.

Then, about a month ago, things shifted, almost into overdrive. I’m sleeping maybe 3-4 hours, but I wake up feeling... wired, not tired. My mind races constantly; I’m talking a mile a minute, bouncing from one idea to the next. My team at the restaurant finds me incredibly irritable – every minor mistake just makes me snap, and I can’t seem to sit still. I'm constantly pacing, fiddling with things, needing to move. The thing is, this constant drive, this impulsivity and my mind jumping all over the place, it all feels like a direct consequence of this gnawing anxiety. It’s like my worries about work, about my divorce, about everything, build up so much that my brain just *has* to go into overdrive, seeking some kind of release."
